integrity: The proof rewrites the perfect Italian condition at a zero cell as row-sum plus column-sum equal to two. This rules out simultaneous zero rows and columns, proves the published optimum values independently, and forces all equality cases. In the rectangular equality case, a zero column yields exactly the one-full-2-column or two-full-1-column families; with no zero column, the weight budget forces n=m+1, one full all-1 row, and a common selected column in every other row. A standalone definition-level verifier checks bounded-weight minimum layers on seven small instances and all predicted constructions in a larger parameter box.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies minimum perfect Italian dominating functions but not the full feasible weight enumerator.
The graph family is restricted to Cartesian products of two complete graphs.
Finite direct verification covers selected small rectangles and construction checks through m=8 and n=9; the arbitrary-parameter result is proved symbolically.
A differently phrased or non-indexed minimum-function classification may exist.
title: Minimum perfect Italian functions of rook graphs
